alternatives.quote: S3 Replication metrics – When you enable S3 Replication metrics, Amazon CloudWatch emits metrics that you can use to track bytes pending, operations pending, and replication latency at the replication rule level. You can view S3 Replication metrics through the Amazon S3 console and the Amazon CloudWatch console. In the Amazon S3 console, you can view these metrics in the source bucket's Metrics tab. evidence_groups.required_fact: Replication metrics track pending bytes, pending operations and replication latency at rule level.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Replication metrics theo dõi bytes đang chờ, operations đang chờ và replication latency ở cấp rule.

alternatives.quote: Replication status values – You can also retrieve the replication status of your objects. The replication status of a replica will return REPLICA.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Source-object replication status can be PENDING, COMPLETED or FAILED; a replica reports REPLICA.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Replication status của source object có thể là PENDING, COMPLETED hoặc FAILED; replica báo REPLICA.

alternatives.quote: To receive replication failure event notifications (s3:Replication:OperationFailedReplication), you must enable S3 Replication metrics on your replication rule. You can enable S3 Replication metrics independently of S3 RTC. For more information, see Enabling S3 Replication metrics.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Failure notifications require replication metrics; S3 RTC is required for threshold-based notifications, not for basic failure notifications.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Thông báo replication thất bại cần bật replication metrics; S3 RTC cần cho thông báo theo ngưỡng, không bắt buộc cho thông báo thất bại cơ bản.

scenarios.reference_answer_vi: Replication metrics theo dõi bytes đang chờ, operations đang chờ và replication latency ở cấp rule. alternatives.quote: Identity-based policies are attached to an IAM user, group, or role. These policies let you specify what that identity can do (its permissions). For example, you can attach the policy to the IAM user named John, stating that he is allowed to perform the Amazon EC2 RunInstances action. The policy could further state that John is allowed to get items from an Amazon DynamoDB table named MyCompany. You can also allow John to manage his own IAM security credentials. Identity-based policies can be managed or inline.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Identity policies attach to IAM users, groups or roles and describe their permissions.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Identity policies gắn với IAM users, groups hoặc roles và mô tả quyền của các identity đó.

alternatives.quote: Resource-based policies are attached to a resource. For example, you can attach resource-based policies to Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon SQS queues, VPC endpoints, AWS Key Management Service encryption keys, Amazon DynamoDB tables and streams, and AWS Sign-In resources. For a list of services that support resource-based policies, see AWS services that work with IAM.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Resource policies attach to supported resources rather than to the requesting identity.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Resource policies gắn với tài nguyên được hỗ trợ thay vì identity đang gửi yêu cầu.

alternatives.quote: Carlos – Carlos can perform list, read, and write actions on Resource Y, but is denied access to Resource Z. The identity-based policy on Carlos allows him to perform list and read actions on Resource Y. The Resource Y resource-based policy also allows him write permissions. However, although his identity-based policy allows him access to Resource Z, the Resource Z resource-based policy denies that access. An explicit Deny overrides an Allow and his access to Resource Z is denied. For more information, see Policy evaluation logic.

evidence_groups.required_fact: An explicit Deny can override an identity-based Allow, so editing an Allow alone need not establish access.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Explicit Deny có thể ghi đè identity-based Allow, vì vậy chỉ sửa Allow chưa chắc đã được truy cập.

scenarios.question_en: A developer can edit an IAM identity policy but not a resource policy. What does each policy type attach to, and why can editing one fail to grant the intended resource access?

scenarios.reference_answer_en: Identity policies attach to IAM users, groups or roles and describe their permissions. Resource policies attach to supported resources rather than to the requesting identity. An explicit Deny can override an identity-based Allow, so editing an Allow alone need not establish access.
scenarios.reference_answer_vi: Identity policies gắn với IAM users, groups hoặc roles và mô tả quyền của các identity đó. Resource policies gắn với tài nguyên được hỗ trợ thay vì identity đang gửi yêu cầu. Explicit Deny có thể ghi đè identity-based Allow, vì vậy chỉ sửa Allow chưa chắc đã được truy cập.

alternatives.quote: For cross-account requests, the requester in the trusted AccountA must have an identity-based policy. That policy must allow them to make a request to the resource in the trusting AccountB. Additionally, the resource-based policy in AccountB must allow the requester in AccountA to access the resource.

evidence_groups.required_fact: The requesting account needs an identity policy allowing the resource access, and the resource account needs a resource policy permitting the requester.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Tài khoản gửi yêu cầu cần identity policy cho phép truy cập tài nguyên, còn tài khoản tài nguyên cần resource policy cho phép requester.

alternatives.quote: When you make a cross-account request, AWS performs two evaluations. AWS evaluates the request in the trusting account and the trusted account. For more information about how a request is evaluated within a single account, see How AWS enforcement code logic evaluates requests to allow or deny access. The request is allowed only if both evaluations return a decision of Allow.

evidence_groups.required_fact: A cross-account request is allowed only when both account evaluations return Allow.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Yêu cầu cross-account chỉ được cho phép khi đánh giá ở cả hai tài khoản đều trả Allow.

scenarios.question_en: Account A grants an identity access to a resource in account B. How must both accounts' policy evaluations permit the cross-account request?
scenarios.question_vi: Tài khoản A cấp cho một identity quyền truy cập tài nguyên của tài khoản B. Việc đánh giá policy ở cả hai tài khoản phải cho phép yêu cầu cross-account như thế nào?
scenarios.reference_answer_en: The requesting account needs an identity policy allowing the resource access, and the resource account needs a resource policy permitting the requester. A cross-account request is allowed only when both account evaluations return Allow.
scenarios.reference_answer_vi: Tài khoản gửi yêu cầu cần identity policy cho phép truy cập tài nguyên, còn tài khoản tài nguyên cần resource policy cho phép requester. Yêu cầu cross-account chỉ được cho phép khi đánh giá ở cả hai tài khoản đều trả Allow.

alternatives.quote: Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is an authorization strategy that defines permissions based on attributes. AWS calls these attributes tags. You can attach tags to IAM resources, including IAM entities (IAM users or IAM roles) and to AWS resources. You can create a single ABAC policy or small set of policies for your IAM principals. You can design ABAC policies that allow operations when the principal's tag matches the resource tag. ABAC's attribute system that provides both high user context and granular access control. Because ABAC is attribute-based, it can perform dynamic authorization for data or applications that grants or revokes access in real time. ABAC is helpful in environments that are scaling and in situations where identity or resource policy management has become complex.

evidence_groups.required_fact: ABAC defines permissions with attributes represented as tags and can compare principal tags with resource tags.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: ABAC định nghĩa quyền theo thuộc tính thể hiện bằng tags và có thể so principal tags với resource tags.

alternatives.quote: For example, you can create three IAM roles with the access-project tag key. Set the tag value of the first IAM role to Heart, the second to Star, and the third to Lightning. You can then use a single policy that allows access when the IAM role and the AWS resource have the tag value access-project. For a detailed tutorial that demonstrates how to use ABAC in AWS, see IAM tutorial: Define permissions to access AWS resources based on tags. To learn about services that support ABAC, see AWS services that work with IAM.

evidence_groups.required_fact: The project-tag example uses matching access-project values for roles and resources, requiring a consistent tagging design.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Ví dụ project tag dùng giá trị access-project khớp nhau giữa roles và resources, đòi hỏi thiết kế tagging nhất quán.

scenarios.question_en: A team wants access rules based on project tags rather than one policy per resource. How does IAM ABAC use principal and resource attributes, and what must the team manage consistently?

scenarios.reference_answer_en: ABAC defines permissions with attributes represented as tags and can compare principal tags with resource tags. The project-tag example uses matching access-project values for roles and resources, requiring a consistent tagging design.
scenarios.reference_answer_vi: ABAC định nghĩa quyền theo thuộc tính thể hiện bằng tags và có thể so principal tags với resource tags. Ví dụ project tag dùng giá trị access-project khớp nhau giữa roles và resources, đòi hỏi thiết kế tagging nhất quán.

alternatives.quote: A key policy is a resource policy for an AWS KMS key. Key policies are the primary way to control access to KMS keys. Every KMS key must have exactly one key policy. The statements in the key policy determine who has permission to use the KMS key and how they can use it. You can also use IAM policies and grants to control access to the KMS key, but every KMS key must have a key policy.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Every KMS key has a key policy, which is the primary access-control mechanism for that key.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Mỗi KMS key có key policy; đây là cơ chế kiểm soát truy cập chính của khóa.

alternatives.quote: Unless the key policy explicitly allows it, you cannot use IAM policies to allow access to a KMS key. Without permission from the key policy, IAM policies that allow permissions have no effect. (You can use an IAM policy to deny a permission to a KMS key without permission from a key policy.) The default key policy enables IAM policies. To enable IAM policies in your key policy, add the policy statement described in Allows access to the AWS account and enables IAM policies.

evidence_groups.required_fact: IAM Allow permissions for a KMS key have no effect unless its key policy enables IAM delegation; IAM Deny can still apply.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: IAM Allow cho KMS key không có hiệu lực nếu key policy chưa cho phép IAM cấp quyền; IAM Deny vẫn có thể áp dụng.

scenarios.reference_answer_en: Every KMS key has a key policy, which is the primary access-control mechanism for that key. IAM Allow permissions for a KMS key have no effect unless its key policy enables IAM delegation; IAM Deny can still apply.
scenarios.reference_answer_vi: Mỗi KMS key có key policy; đây là cơ chế kiểm soát truy cập chính của khóa. IAM Allow cho KMS key không có hiệu lực nếu key policy chưa cho phép IAM cấp quyền; IAM Deny vẫn có thể áp dụng.

alternatives.quote: When your Lambda Event Function encounters an error while processing a batch, all messages in that batch become visible in the queue again by default, including messages that Lambda processed successfully. As a result, your function can end up processing the same message several times.

evidence_groups.required_fact: By default, one failed SQS batch can make all its messages visible again, including successfully processed messages.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Theo mặc định, batch SQS bị lỗi có thể làm mọi message hiện lại, kể cả message đã xử lý thành công.

alternatives.quote: To avoid reprocessing successfully processed messages in a failed batch, you can configure your event source mapping to make only the failed messages visible again. This is called a partial batch response. To turn on partial batch responses, specify ReportBatchItemFailures for the FunctionResponseTypes action when configuring your event source mapping. With this setting, your function can return a partial success, which can help reduce the number of unnecessary retries on records.

evidence_groups.required_fact: Configure ReportBatchItemFailures so a partial batch response makes only the failed messages visible again.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Cấu hình ReportBatchItemFailures để partial batch response chỉ làm các message thất bại hiện lại.

scenarios.reference_answer_en: By default, one failed SQS batch can make all its messages visible again, including successfully processed messages. Configure ReportBatchItemFailures so a partial batch response makes only the failed messages visible again.

alternatives.quote: To allow your function time to process each batch of records, set the source queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the configuration timeout on your function. The extra time allows Lambda to retry if your function is throttled while processing a previous batch.

evidence_groups.required_fact: The documentation recommends a visibility timeout at least six times the function timeout to leave room for throttling retries.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Tài liệu khuyến nghị visibility timeout ít nhất gấp sáu lần function timeout để có thời gian retry khi throttling.

alternatives.quote: Your function's timeout must be less than or equal to the queue's visibility timeout. Lambda validates this requirement when you create or update an event source mapping and returns an error if the function timeout exceeds the queue's visibility timeout.

evidence_groups.required_fact: The function timeout must not exceed the queue visibility timeout; Lambda validates this for event source mappings.

Enable Kinesis streaming on the DynamoDB table by using the DynamoDB enable-kinesis-streaming-destination command. aws dynamodb enable-kinesis-streaming-destination \

  --stream-arn arn:aws:kinesis:us-west-2:12345678901:stream/samplestream
  --enable-kinesis-streaming-configuration ApproximateCreationDateTimePrecision=MICROSECOND

aws dynamodb enable-kinesis-streaming-destination \
  --table-name Music \
  --stream-arn arn:aws:kinesis:us-west-2:12345678901:stream/samplestream

alternatives.quote: Use a redrive policy to specify the maxReceiveCount. alternatives.quote: For standard queues, the expiration of a message is always based on its original enqueue timestamp. When a message is moved to a dead-letter queue, the enqueue timestamp is unchanged. The ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric indicates when the message moved to the dead-letter queue, not when the message was originally sent. For example, assume that a message spends 1 day in the original queue before it's moved to a dead-letter queue. If the dead-letter queue's retention period is 4 days, the message is deleted from the dead-letter queue after 3 days and the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage is 3 days. Thus, it is a best practice to always set the retention period of a dead-letter queue to be longer than the retention period of the original queue.

evidence_groups.required_fact: For standard queues, the original enqueue timestamp is retained in the DLQ, so its retention should exceed the source queue's retention.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Với standard queue, message giữ enqueue timestamp gốc khi vào DLQ, nên retention của DLQ cần dài hơn source queue.

alternatives.quote: For FIFO queues, the enqueue timestamp resets when the message is moved to a dead-letter queue. The ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric indicates when the message moved to the dead-letter queue. In the same example above, the message is deleted from the dead-letter queue after four days and the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage is four days.

evidence_groups.required_fact: For FIFO queues, moving to a DLQ resets the enqueue timestamp, unlike standard queues.
evidence_groups.required_fact_vi: Với FIFO queue, enqueue timestamp được đặt lại khi chuyển vào DLQ, khác standard queue.

A target is a resource or endpoint that EventBridge sends an event to when the event matches the event pattern defined for a rule. The rule processes the event data and sends the pertinent information to the target. To deliver event data to a target, EventBridge needs permission to access the target resource. When you add targets to a rule and that rule runs soon after, any new or updated targets might not be immediately invoked. Allow a short period of time for changes to take effect.

This topic describes targets for Custom Event Bus - Classic rules. On the Custom Event Bus, a target belongs to a subscriber rather than a rule.
